In the permanganate ion ($\text{MnO}_4^-$), the manganese atom is in the +7 oxidation state. The electronic configuration of Mn(VII) is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^0$. 

Ligand-field splitting parameters ($Dq$) and Racah parameters ($B$ and $C$) are used to describe the energy levels and transitions of electrons within the $d$-orbitals (d-d transitions). Because Mn(VII) has no electrons in its $3d$ shell, d-d transitions are impossible.

The intense absorption bands observed at $17\,570\text{ cm}^{-1}$, $31\,560\text{ cm}^{-1}$, and $38\,320\text{ cm}^{-1}$ have very high molar extinction coefficients ($\epsilon > 1\,000\text{ M}^{-1}\text{cm}^{-1}$), which is characteristic of allowed transitions. These are identified as ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) transitions, where electrons move from the oxygen $2p$ orbitals to the empty manganese $3d$ orbitals. 

Since the observed spectrum consists of charge-transfer bands rather than d-d transitions, it is not possible to determine the ligand-field splitting parameter $Dq$ or the Racah parameter $B$ using this data.
